analysis.investment_thesis: Helloji Holidays is a tiny INR 39 Cr micro-cap travel agency with a negligible 0.51% ROE trading at 18.8x earnings — the valuation assumes quality that the fundamentals do not demonstrate. This is a speculative SME-style listing, not a steady compounder, and fails nearly every quality filter I apply.
key_strengths: Promoter holding reasonably high at 69.97% — skin in the game
Asset-light tours/travel business with no obvious debt red flags at this size
Some institutional interest (FII 5.81%, DII 8.40%) for a micro-cap
key_risks: ROE of 0.51% is effectively zero — business is not earning its cost of capital
Tiny 39 Cr market cap in a fragmented, commoditized travel segment with no moat
P/E of 18.8x is expensive given sub-1% returns; earnings base is too small to be meaningful
red_flags: ROE far below my 15% minimum threshold
Micro-cap BSE listing with limited disclosure and liquidity
No dividend track record visible; no multi-year consistency demonstrated
analysis.detailed_analysis:
At a 0.51% ROE, Helloji is destroying value versus any risk-free benchmark — a fixed deposit beats it comfortably. The tours and travel industry is brutally competitive, dominated by MakeMyTrip, Yatra, EaseMyTrip and countless local operators, with no pricing power for a 39 Cr player. At 18.8x P/E on such weak earnings, the market cap is essentially a lottery ticket on future growth rather than a reflection of current cash generation. This is precisely the kind of glamour-adjacent, hype-driven micro-cap I consistently avoid.

My framework demands ROE >15%, consistent 10-15% revenue CAGR, strong free cash flow, and a dividend record — Helloji shows none of this. Promoter holding at ~70% is the only tick mark. Until this business demonstrates several years of 15%+ ROE, disciplined capital allocation, and earnings visibility, there is no reason to own it. I would rather wait decades for the right price on a quality name than take a flyer here.
